title: Quantum Formulation of Chiral Vortical Effect in Weyl Semi-metals
abstract: The chiral vortical effect (CVE) is the generation of an axial current in a rotating Weyl fermion; its description is presently based on semiclassical frameworks. In this work, we develop a fully quantum formulation for CVE, solving the exact evolution of microscopic spinful wavefunctions, which enables a bottom-up quantitative test of semi-classical theories and postulated distributions $f_{\text{CVE}}$ in different reference frames. Notably, it shows that $f_{\text{CVE}}$ is over a ground-state-free Floquet spectrum, qualitatively distinct from a thermal equilibrium distribution (i.e., fermi form $f_F$), underscoring CVE as a non-equilibrium phenomenon, distinguished from other chiral transports. The $f_F$ only approximately holds when three conditions are simultaneously fulfilled: (1) slow rotation $ωR/v_F\ll 1$, (2) high chemical potential $μ/(\hbar v_F R)\gg 1$, (3) isotropic symmetry, where $R$ is the size, $v_F$ is fermi velocity. In these conditions, the theory recovers established semiclassical results, including the current-response coefficients and the magnetization contribution; otherwise, it uncovers quantum phenomena such as ``void states", deviation from the semiclassical formula $j_{\text{CVE}} \sim μ^2$, a $v_F$-independent charge pumping. The theory is based on semimetals, providing more experimentally accessible detection than fundamental Weyl particles.
summary: This work pioneers a fully quantum description of the Chiral Vortical Effect (CVE) using Weyl semimetals. By solving for microscopic wavefunctions rather than relying on semiclassical distributions, the authors prove that CVE is fundamentally a non-equilibrium process. This provides a powerful tool to detect genuine quantum transport phenomena in materials.
main_problem: To develop a fully quantum formulation for the Chiral Vortical Effect (CVE), moving beyond existing semiclassical descriptions.
main_result: The CVE distribution is shown to be over a ground-state-free Floquet spectrum, confirming it as a non-equilibrium phenomenon distinct from thermal equilibrium. The theory also predicts novel quantum effects when semi-classical approximations fail.
method: The authors solve the exact evolution of microscopic spinful wavefunctions using a time-dependent Hamiltonian approach and compare results against established semiclassical kinetic theories.
model_or_system: The study uses Weyl semimetals as an experimentally accessible platform. The system is modeled by a non-relativistic quantum Hamiltonian incorporating chiral fermion dynamics and an axial rotation term ($\hat{V}$).
key_observables: Axial current ($j_z$), energy spectrum ($\epsilon$), and the quantum distribution function ($\hat{f}_{CVE}$)
important_parameters: Rotation frequency ($\omega$), Fermi velocity ($v_F$), Chemical potential ($\mu$), System size ($R$)
main_assumptions: The semiclassical approximation is only valid under three strict conditions: slow rotation, high chemical potential, and isotropic symmetry.
figures_summary: Figure 2 compares the energy spectra for the non-rotating case ($\omega=0$) versus the rotating case ($H$), showing Floquet-type spectral features.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for a quantum formulation, deriving the Hamiltonian respecting physical symmetries (like observer rotation invariance), calculating observables using wavefunctions in Hilbert space, and finally comparing these results to known semi-classical limits.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter transport, the core methodology involves non-equilibrium dynamics, Floquet theory, and the rigorous comparison between quantum evolution and classical/statistical approximations, which are central themes in open quantum systems.
